idea-plugin.name: TestInsanity
idea-plugin.description:
Rename a class and its tests are renamed with it. Jump from a method straight to the method that tests it. TestInsanity learns your naming convention instead of guessing at it.


Rename the subject, and the matching test class and test methods are proposed with their new names.

Why not just Navigate -> Test?
Because it guesses one hardcoded class name and stops there. TestInsanity works from a convention you declare, matches methods as well as classes, goes in both directions, and carries renames through.

  ${className}Test   maps Color to ColorTest
  test${subjectName}*   maps isDarkColor() to testIsDarkColor_whenBlack()

Nothing to set up: ${className}Test and ${className}IT are configured on install. Each scheme binds one class convention to the method conventions used inside it, and schemes are tried in order — so unit tests, integration tests and specs coexist in one project, each with its own method naming.

  • Renaming, both ways — subject class to test classes, test class to subject, subject method to test methods, test method to subject. Renames appear in the standard Rename related items dialog, so you can deselect any of them.
  • Navigation to the method — Jump to Sibling (CTRL+ALT+`) moves between a method and its test method, not only between their classes. Navigate -> Test (CTRL+SHIFT+T) follows the same scheme.
  • Gutter icons — at the class and at the method, the sibling on the other side, its JUnit 5 DisplayName when it has one, and a distinct icon for a test with no subject.
  • Alt+Enter creates what is missing — the test class, or the test method with the right framework annotation, one entry per scheme. On a test, the same key creates the subject. New classes land in the correct test root, including when tests live in a module of their own.
  • Your convention in version control — a .testinsanity.json at the project root pins the scheme for the whole team, the way .editorconfig does. Keys it declares win and show as disabled in the settings; keys it omits stay personal. It is re-read on every change, including branch switches, and gets completion, documentation and validation as you type. One click creates it from the settings you already have.

Every method links to the method that tests it, and the ones with no test stay unmarked.


Every class links to its test class, and a test with no subject gets an icon of its own.

Also handles JUnit 4, JUnit 5 and TestNG including nested, parameterized and templated tests, any annotation composed of theirs, a house annotation named outright or by package wildcard, Kotlin with backtick test names (optional dependency, K2 ready), inherited and abstract test classes, and optional @DisplayName generation and sync.

Configured per project under Settings -> Tools -> TestInsanity.

Report an issue
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v2.0.0

New
  • Project configuration in .testinsanity.json at the project root, so the naming scheme lives in version control instead of in .idea. Keys the file declares win over the IDE settings and appear disabled in the settings dialog; keys it omits stay personal. The file is re-read whenever it changes, including on branch switches, and a bundled JSON schema gives it completion, inline documentation and validation. Settings -> Tools -> TestInsanity shows whether the file is in use, can switch it off per IDE, and can create it from the settings you already have.
  • Renaming works in all four directions: subject class to test classes, test class to subject class, subject method to test methods, and test method to subject method.
  • Renaming goes through the standard Rename related items dialog, so it also applies to in-place rename and lets you deselect any proposed rename.
  • Several named schemes per project, listed and reordered in the settings and tried top to bottom. Each scheme binds one test class pattern to its own test method patterns, so unit, integration and end to end tests keep separate naming instead of sharing one flat list. The first scheme whose test class pattern matches wins, and an existing single-pattern setup migrates into one scheme with no change in behaviour.
  • Navigate -> Test follows the configured naming scheme, and the Create Test Sibling intention creates the class and method your scheme names.
  • New intention (Alt+Enter): create the missing test class or test method for the subject. One entry per scheme that is still missing its test class, so a unit scheme and an integration scheme can each be created; a chooser appears when more than one is missing.
  • The reverse intention (Alt+Enter): create the missing subject class from a test class, and the missing subject method when the scheme names it unambiguously.
  • Created classes land in the module test root, or in the module declared as its test module, or in the single dependent module that has test roots, so a separate test module is handled.
  • JUnit 5 nested test classes are matched.
  • The test annotation check follows composed annotations, so a project-local @IntegrationTest that is itself annotated @Test is recognized, as is an override of an annotated method. Every JUnit Platform engine is covered through @Testable, and additionalTestAnnotations declares a house runner by name or by package wildcard.
  • Patterns accept spaces, for Kotlin backtick test names, with a matching preset.
  • Optional @DisplayName generation and rename synchronization.
  • Gutter icons are computed off the highlighting pass and cached, appear in every JVM language, and can be switched off in Settings -> Editor -> General -> Gutter Icons.
Fixed
  • Renaming a subject class did not rename its test classes.
  • Renaming a test class or a test method did not rename its subject.
  • A test living in its own module never resolved its subject.
  • Which sibling was picked followed index order and could differ between runs.
  • A test method was counted twice when two matching test classes were related by inheritance.
  • A nested helper class inside a test class was reported as a test of the outer subject.
  • The settings Apply button ignored changes to the renaming checkbox.
  • A damaged TestInsanity.xml could leave the plugin inert.
  • Creating .testinsanity.json from the settings wrote an empty array the plugin then refused to read.
  • A settings file that named test frameworks explicitly did not pick up annotations added by an upgrade.
  • Gutter icons kept the previous scheme in already-open editors until the file was edited again.
  • The method gutter tooltip read TestMethod and SubjectMethod with no space.
  • Only the first scheme could create its test class; once any scheme had one, the others could not.
Changed
  • Show renaming dialog is now Pre-select test renames: it decides whether the proposed renames start checked rather than whether a dialog appears, and the dialog is the platform Rename related items dialog. Settings written by earlier versions carry over with renaming left on.

v1.3.0
  • 2026.1+
  • Kotlin K2 mode support.
  • Kotlin support is now optional: the plugin works without the Kotlin plugin.
  • Jump to Sibling now falls back to the class when a Kotlin function has no matching JVM method.
  • Fixed errors when renaming Kotlin functions that have no matching JVM method.
